beats.fact: Brazil captain Raphinha was sent off on the touchline after he had already been substituted, along with Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti, as Japan beat Brazil 3-2 in a friendly in Singapore on Saturday 14 November 2026.
Brazil had knocked Japan out of this summer's World Cup in the round of 32. In the rematch Barcelona's Raphinha was made Brazil captain for the day.

Japan led 2-0 inside the first 19 minutes through Takefusa Kubo (15') and Keito Nakamura (19'). Vinícius Júnior scored either side of half-time to make it 2-2. Raphinha was substituted, with Endrick coming on for him.

In the 91st minute (first minute of stoppage time) Coventry's Tatsuhiro Sakamoto poked in Japan's winner. Brazil wanted a foul on João Gomes in the build-up; Ancelotti and the already-substituted Raphinha protested on the touchline and both were sent off. Ancelotti blamed the referee's inexperience.

numbers.winner_minute: 91st minute / first minute of injury time

beats.quote: The referee gave me a red card because he said I wasn't able to control the bench, and that all the players were on the field. The result, obviously, was influenced by the referee's performance. But it's not his fault. It was a high-level match and I don't think he had the experience to handle this kind of game.

beats.fact: Three days later, on Tuesday 17 November, Raphinha and Ancelotti watched from the stands as Brazil thrashed Singapore 7-0, with a Vinícius Júnior hat-trick inside 21 minutes.
